conservation.help_by: Keep nesting beaches dark and clear; support marine protected areas.
conservation.caution_against: Never buy turtle products; don’t block crawlways or touch nesting turtles.

life_info.eating: Crabs, conchs, and other crunchy invertebrates. Big head and jaws crack shells other turtles can’t.
life_info.mating: Famous nesting beaches; females may travel huge distances.
life_info.habitat: Open ocean and coastal bays; powerful jaws for hard prey. Solitary travelers between feeding and nesting grounds.

fun_facts: The logger head is packed with muscle for shell-cracking.
Hatchlings use Earth’s magnetic field like a built-in GPS.

conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Algae — a key grazer that helps coral stay clear. Night grazing marches across reef rock.
life_info.mating: Broadcast spawners; larvae drift before settling.
life_info.habitat: Reef crevices and rocky bottoms; spines wave in the surge. A 1980s die-off changed Caribbean reefs — recovery still matters.

fun_facts: Step carefully: spines are brittle and painful.
When Diadema vanish, algae can smother coral.
